original_question: From what height would you need to drop a steak for it to be cooked when it hit the ground?
short_answer_summary: Reentry can sear or ablate the surface, but the interior stays raw and the long cold final descent can freeze the steak.
detailed_scientific_explanation: The author simulates an 8-ounce steak using hockey-puck drag and missile-reentry heating research, then compares heating duration with cookbook guidance. Compressive heating becomes important above roughly Mach 2. A steak released from rest accelerates until it enters thicker atmosphere at roughly 30–50 km, then slows to terminal speed. Regardless of initial height, the final 25 km takes six or seven minutes in mostly subfreezing air. A 39 km release is subsonic; about 50 km is needed to break the sound barrier. At 70 km the steak briefly encounters air at about 350°F, insufficient to cook it. At 100 km it spends around 90 seconds above Mach 2, but heating is soon replaced by cold airflow. At 250 km it can reach Mach 6 and sear outside, while remaining raw inside. Higher starts cause charring and ablation; sustained exposure removes material rather than producing a cooked intact steak. A Pittsburgh-rare result is the closest outcome.
initial_assumptions: 8-ounce filet modeled approximately as a hockey puck
Released from rest, not already moving at orbital speed
Lower-speed tumbling and a stable squashed hypersonic shape are speculative

quantitative_facts.value: 30–50 km deceleration region; six or seven minutes for final 25 km; terminal speed about 30 m/s
39 km subsonic; ~50 km sound barrier; 70 km about 350°F for under one minute; 100 km about 90 s above Mach 2
250 km release reaches Mach 6; shock layer at greater heights reaches thousands of degrees

footnotes.note: Probably fine after landing on water, mud, or leaves means intact, not necessarily safe to eat.
Van Allen belt exposure is too short to sterilize the steak.

uncertainties_and_limitations: Author explicitly calls hypersonic shape assumption a wild guess; no steak wind-tunnel data found
Intact landing is not food-safety validation
extraction_notes: Source transcript is machine OCR and requires line-by-line proofreading against page images.
